title: A Friendly Star in the Flame

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Sit comfortably with the flame near eye level. Keep your face and jaw relaxed. Blink whenever you need to, and stop if you notice pain, dizziness, or persistent eye discomfort.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let your gaze meet the centre of the flame without drilling into it. Imagine a friendly little star has come close enough to visit.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice colour near the wick... the brighter edge... and the faint glow around it. Keep the eyes soft. Blinking is part of seeing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] When attention wanders, return to one small detail in the flame. No need to freeze the rest of the world.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Let this be steady rather than severe. A star does not ask the sky to strain around it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now close your eyes gently. Notice whether an after-image appears behind the eyelids. It may be bright, faint, colourful, moving, or absent.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If an image is present, observe it without trying to hold it still. Let it drift like a tiny satellite across the dark.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If there is no image, rest with the darkness itself. The practice does not require a visual effect.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel the breath and the contact points beneath you while the inner sky changes on its own.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet room ambience] [softly] Open your eyes and return to the flame. Let the gaze land lightly, as though recognising an old friend across a quiet room.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice movement inside apparent stillness. The flame leans, recovers, brightens, and narrows while remaining itself.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest attention at the wick for a while. Blink naturally. Each return can be gentle and immediate.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the flame be the only small task for these next few breaths... a warm point of light in a wide and patient night.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Close your eyes once more. Notice the remembered flame, the after-image, or simply the space where it had been.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Imagine the little star becoming quieter and more distant. You do not need to preserve it. Let fading be part of the meditation.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Broaden attention to the whole face, the whole body, and the sounds in the room. Allow the eyes to rest completely.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Rub the hands together if that feels pleasant, then open your eyes slowly. Leave the flame behind and carry the steadiness.
